title: loss-aware-prefetch-controller-and-quant-adaptive-fallback
author: Marcus Nguyen
description: Motivation: We observed bursty degradation in unit economics during traffic spikes where prefill/prefetch heuristics overfilled KV caches and aggressive quant tiers caused quality regressions. This PR introduces a loss-aware prefetch controller that trades small latency overhead for measurable token-cost savings while avoiding deterministic quality drops via an adaptive quant fallback policy. Summary of changes: 1) Add a new prefetch controller that uses a short-loss metric window (cross-entropy on eval prompts) to decide whether to prefill KV caches for large requests and enable opportunistic microbatching, 2) Introduce a quant adaptive fallback that can automatically step down quant aggressive paths if the loss window crosses a threshold, 3) Integrate unit-econ telemetry hooks for per-route token-cost and quality correlation charts, 4) Add an opt-in runtime flag and a Canary experiment harness to run this logic under controlled traffic, 5) Add regression and perf tests plus benchmark vectors. Why this approach: Prior autotuners focussed only on latency or raw cost; this controller provides an explicit signal to avoid quant-induced quality regressions during workload shifts while still allowing cost-saving prefetching when model output quality is stable. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in PR description (Linear ENG-3421) - [x] Unit tests for controller logic - [x] End-to-end canary harness + traffic replay - [x] Perf benchmarks against main for 512/2048 token shapes - [x] Telemetry dashboards added - [x] Docs snippet in runtime/README about opt-in flag Runtime impact and data: - Default off for hosted customers; enabled in Dedicated experimental channel only. - Local perf on a 4xA100 pool: cost per 1k tokens down ~8.3% for conversational workloads with 60% cache hit profile, median p95 token latency increase +12ms in worst-case shapes. - On adversarial eval prompts, quant-adaptive fallback prevented a BLEU-like quality drop of ~4.6 points compared to always-on aggressive quant. Testing and CI: - Added unit tests for the loss window smoothing and threshold logic. - Integrated canary pipeline that replays production traces from the last 48h (sanitized). - CI initially failed lint due to style in prefetch module; fixed in second commit. Related work and follow-ups: - Pair with the upcoming econ-policy CLI to expose safe thresholds to SREs - Follow-up PR: auto-calibration of the loss-window threshold using historical eval sets Commits summary: - cf7b1e8 implement loss-aware prefetch controller and interface hooks - d41a02f add quant-adaptive fallback and policy registry - 4f9c1b2 telemetry: add unit-econ metrics and dashboard links - b3e2ffa tests: add unit + e2e canary harness and sample traces - 8a7d9c0 docs: runtime README and canary runbook How to review: - Focus on the controller state machine and the threshold gating semantics in prefetch/controller.go - Verify telemetry names and labels match the observability-pack conventions in observability/metrics.yaml - Run the canary harness locally with 'tools/canary/run --replay sample-traces/2025-01-14.json' Performance numbers and benchmarks are in perf/benchmarks/README.md. Merge notes: Squash merged after green CI and approvals from Aisha and Sofia. Incident linkage: This work was kickstarted by INT-827 where a Dedicated customer experienced cost spikes during scaling modes. Security: No secrets or new network endpoints. Rollout plan: staged canary in Dedicated->region-us-west->global if metrics hold.

release_notes: Introduce loss-aware prefetcher with quant-adaptive fallback to reduce token costs while protecting quality regressions; opt-in experimental feature for Dedicated; performance: ~8% token cost improvement under typical chat workloads; added canary harness and new unit-econ telemetry.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: feature behind opt-in flag and Dedicated canary only. The short loss-window is tuned to prioritize quality over raw cost; follow-ups will explore automatic threshold learning and exposing safe defaults for hosted plans.
